one_line: AI kitchen manager that unifies inventory, recipes, expiry awareness, and grocery planning.
what_it_does: Tracks kitchen ingredients and uses an agent to recommend recipes and manage grocery needs.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to inventory, expiry dates, recipes, quantities, and grocery state plausibly removes substantial copy-paste and screen-navigation friction, though the same outcome is possible with UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes structured tools for inspecting inventory, expiry dates, recipes, quantities, and grocery planning.
Example request combines expiring ingredients, recipe selection, serving scaling, and grocery-list mutation.
execution_rationale: The concept and claimed workflow are coherent, but no video or usable product frames were submitted; the Devpost screenshot's embedded media is blocked, so end-to-end execution cannot be verified.
execution_evidence: FACTS reports video=False and five gallery images.
Devpost screenshot shows blocked embedded media rather than the product workflow.
impact_rationale: Home cooks have a concrete recurring problem in coordinating inventory, expiry, recipes, and shopping; the described unified workflow directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies separated kitchen information and manual comparison as the target problem.
The stated use case produces a recipe and updates a shopping list from actual inventory.
creativity_rationale: A sensible, useful synthesis of pantry tracking, recipe planning, and agent actions, with limited evidence of a novel interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Unifies several traditionally separate kitchen-management surfaces.
Positions WebMCP structured state as the core convenience.
usability_note: The intended natural-language workflow is approachable, but interface usability is not visually evidenced.
red_flags: No submitted video or accessible visual product evidence.
Execution claims rely largely on truncated prose.
standouts: Strong concrete end-to-end kitchen-management use case.
advance_reason: Good concept and impact, but the packet lacks sufficient execution evidence for advancement.

one_line: A WebMCP/OAuth workflow for turning AI workspaces into publishable, monetizable artifacts.
what_it_does: Uses cloud workspaces to draft, edit, diff, build, snapshot, publish, and close content projects.
leverage_rationale: The claimed typed workspace lifecycle, schema-aware edits, diff/build gating, snapshots, and publishing are materially more reliable than an agent clicking a generic editor, though the evidence is packaging-heavy.
leverage_evidence: Screenshot/video thumbnail shows start workspace, read and update paper.md, source diff, build, snapshot, publish, and close steps.
ABOUT identifies WebMCP and controlled workspace operations.
execution_rationale: The visible packaging presents a coherent lifecycle but is a paused thumbnail and does not independently establish successful publication or live output.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly contains a paused OAuth/MCP demo thumbnail.
Thumbnail text claims successful diff/build gating, but no independently checked final artifact is shown.
impact_rationale: There is plausible value for authors, seminar operators, and creators who need repeatable content publishing and monetization workflows, but the audience/problem fit is only lightly articulated.
impact_evidence: Pitch explicitly targets business cards and monetization for books and live seminars.
Workflow includes a complete content publication lifecycle.
creativity_rationale: Combining AI workspace monetization with schema-aware, lifecycle-controlled publishing is a fresh synthesis and ambitious integration.
creativity_evidence: The person-facing concept spans workspace creation, source editing, build validation, snapshotting, and publishing.
OAuth/MCP cloud workspace orchestration is more ambitious than a simple chat wrapper.
usability_note: The workflow is explicit and gated, but the actual user experience is not demonstrated live.
red_flags: Evidence is a paused embedded demo and truncated text; successful end state is not independently clear.
standouts: Detailed publication lifecycle with source-diff and build gating.
advance_reason: Promising and ambitious, but insufficiently verified execution evidence.

one_line: A policy-governed system where analysts author dynamic agent tools over sensitive internal reports.
what_it_does: Lets an analyst perform a report once, approve it into a typed tool, and enforce page-level disclosure and schema policies.
leverage_rationale: The page dynamically exposes tools authored from live work, shares structured state with the agent, validates permissible fields, and removes stale tools; this is central and difficult to replicate comparably with UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Transcript says the report runner writes the tool and the page decides what may leave.
Transcript describes getTools/registerTool, policy refusal of National ID, approvals, generated edge cases, and fingerprint-based removal.
Video frames show report UI, restricted-field warning, and terminal/tool inspection.
execution_rationale: The 177-second video transcript and frame sheets together show a coherent operational workflow from manual report to tool proposal, policy checks, approval, invocation, and stale-tool handling.
execution_evidence: Video is 177 seconds and transcript describes live report controls, grouping, denied fields, approval, and registered tool execution.
Frame sheets show the dashboard, numeric results, restricted-data states, and technical tool inspection.
Devpost packaging and about text agree on the same controlled-tool thesis.
impact_rationale: This addresses a real enterprise problem: enabling useful agent automation over sensitive internal data without exposing identifiers or bypassing authorization.
impact_evidence: The stated payroll/report scenario includes 1,680 rows and explicit National ID restrictions.
Policy layer comparison claims 0 identifiers returned versus 1,552 without policy.
Human confirmation and audit semantics are described throughout.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic, analyst-authored tools with page-owned disclosure policy and schema fingerprints are an original and deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Tool surface is not fixed at build time.
A demonstrated report becomes an approved tool, with generated edge cases and invalidation on schema drift.
usability_note: The workflow makes permissions, confirmation, and tool meaning visible, though it is designed for an internal analyst context.
standouts: Concrete privacy-preserving behavior is shown and narrated.
Schema drift and approval are treated as first-class product state.
advance_reason: Strongest packet: transformative WebMCP leverage, credible enterprise impact, and unusually complete evidence.

one_line: An asymmetric bomb-defusal game where the human sees the device and the agent holds the manual and tools.
what_it_does: Creates cooperative timed puzzles requiring a human to describe visual signals while an agent consults manuals and acts through constrained tools.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the game mechanic: it deliberately partitions visual perception and structured manual/tool access between human and agent, making cooperation impossible to reproduce comparably with ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says the human sees the bomb while the agent has manual, scanner, and tools but cannot see/hear the screen.
ABOUT defines the Describe → Look up → Decide → Confirm → Act loop and changing tool set.
Frame sheet shows timed console, assistant panel, DEVICE DISARMED, and Crossed Wires states.
execution_rationale: Frames show a coherent timed console, puzzle modules, assistant channel, successful DEVICE DISARMED state, and progression to Crossed Wires; exact live agent invocation is not present in a transcript.
execution_evidence: Contact sheet visibly shows active timed device-disarming interface.
Repeated completion frames read DEVICE DISARMED.
Devpost screenshot shows the product briefing and tool-line/status claims.
impact_rationale: The game has clear entertainment and cooperative-learning value, and the human-agent communication constraint is credible for its intended audience.
impact_evidence: ABOUT explicitly frames cooperative bomb-defusal play, communication, and escape-room inspiration.
Frames show timed missions and a completed device state.
creativity_rationale: The asymmetric human/AI abilities and conversation-as-gameplay model are highly original, memorable, and pursued through the core mechanics.
creativity_evidence: Agent is intentionally denied visual perception while receiving machine-readable manual/tools.
Human and agent each lack the complete capability set; neither can defuse alone.
usability_note: The briefing, task modules, timer, and clear completion state suggest a playable flow; text legibility limits detailed assessment.
red_flags: No transcript, so actual agent tool invocation is not directly evidenced.
standouts: WebMCP boundary is the central game mechanic, not an integration afterthought.
advance_reason: Highly creative, product-coherent asymmetric game with strong WebMCP leverage and visible completion evidence.

one_line: A living mystery manuscript whose discoveries unlock new agent actions and narrative consequences.
what_it_does: Combines authored interactive fiction, canonical story state, progressive tool disclosure, and agent-mediated natural-language play.
leverage_rationale: The story's causal progression controls the agent's live tool surface, enabling a stateful authored mystery that is difficult to preserve through generic UI guessing or an unconstrained chatbot.
leverage_evidence: Frames explicitly show 'The story changes what the agent can do' and a live-tab action with schema.
Tool cards show 3 initial tools, Pencil found, and a newly unlocked action.
ABOUT says page protects secrets, commits consequences, and reveals structured verbs when earned.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent authored mystery, manuscript clue, pencil-triggered memory, contradiction discovery, and progressive tool states; absence of transcript reduces certainty about actual agent calls.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show 'Once Upon', locked-room setup, North Station question, manuscript, pencil discovery, and progressively revealed actions.
Devpost screenshot identifies a WebMCP demo and living-manuscript product.
ABOUT describes one complete authored mystery, The Last Manuscript.
impact_rationale: Interactive fiction audiences have a clear desire for free-form play with authored mystery structure; the product directly addresses the tradeoff between improvisation and clue discipline.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies rigid menus versus unconstrained AI stories as the problem.
Frames visibly show a mystery clue, memory reconstruction, and official-story contradiction.
creativity_rationale: Progressive narrative-earned agent capabilities are a genuinely novel interaction model, with the mechanic integrated deeply into authored story causality.
creativity_evidence: Discovering and using a pencil changes canonical story state and reveals the next action.
The agent sees only what the story has earned, rather than a static global tool list.
usability_note: Natural-language play and visible manuscript/tool progression are compelling, though the full interaction loop is inferred from frames and description.
red_flags: No transcript; tool-call behavior is shown through captions and state cards rather than directly readable invocation logs.
standouts: Narrative causality and WebMCP tool registration are fused into one memorable mechanic.
advance_reason: Distinctive agent-native fiction with strong visual evidence of progressive disclosure and authored consequences.

one_line: A local-first spreadsheet cleaning studio with shared human and agent tools, previews, approvals, attribution, and undo.
what_it_does: Loads messy CSV data, analyzes quality issues, proposes fixes, and applies reversible human-approved transformations.
leverage_rationale: Shared typed tools, previews, approvals, attribution, reversibility, and local DuckDB state make agent data mutation substantially safer and more precise than generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Pitch claims human and agent use the same 15 WebMCP tools.
ABOUT describes eight concurrent analyzers, measurement-backed findings, preview-before-write, approval, attribution, and undo.
Frames show upload/validation, messy-sales-data dashboard, quality metrics, workflow feed, and logs.
execution_rationale: The visual packet shows a consistent upload-to-dataset-health-to-workflow/logs product, while the description supplies a coherent safety architecture; exact end-to-end cleaning result is only partially shown.
execution_evidence: Frames show CSV/JSON upload, dataset detail, quality metrics, suggested next steps, activity/workflow panel, and logs.
Devpost screenshot states local-first execution and previewed, approved, attributed, reversible changes.
No gallery images, but frame sheets provide product-motion evidence.
impact_rationale: Data cleaning is a widespread, costly task and the product targets the key trust barriers—measurement, review, attribution, reversibility, and local privacy.
impact_evidence: ABOUT names mixed dates, duplicates, currency strings, whitespace, outliers, and parser-dropped rows.
Local DuckDB/WASM and separately gated external communication address privacy and control.
creativity_rationale: Human-agent co-editing with a shared execution path and reversible, attributed transformations is a strong synthesis beyond a generic AI cleaning assistant.
creativity_evidence: No separate agent path: buttons and tools share the same handlers.
Every proposed change carries measurement and is previewed before approval.
usability_note: The upload, health, suggested-next-step, and logs structure suggests a legible workflow for a complex task.
red_flags: No transcript and no gallery images; final cleaned export/result is not clearly visible.
standouts: Strong safety model for agent-mediated data mutation.
Local-first architecture and shared human/agent path.
advance_reason: Credible, high-impact data workflow with strong leverage and visible product-state evidence.

one_line: A timed asymmetric arcade game where a human operates a console and an AI agent reads the manual.
what_it_does: Uses scoped WebMCP tools, typed manual access, text communication, and bounded actions to make delegation the game.
leverage_rationale: The protocol boundary creates the central information asymmetry: structured manual access for the agent and physical controls for the human, with scoped tools becoming game state.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT says the agent must not inspect the screen and receives procedures, charts, codebooks, clock, and text channel.
Each act registers scoped tools with AbortSignal and removes them when it ends.
Human controls normal presses; consequential actions require confirmation.
execution_rationale: The 159-second video plus coherent description establish a designed five-act, ten-minute, three-strike game with bounded controls, though no transcript reduces direct verification of the run.
execution_evidence: FACTS reports a 159-second video and three frame sheets.
Frame sheets show CrossTalk/Handshake onboarding, timed dashboard, task board, and device-disarm completion.
ABOUT specifies act-scoped tool lifecycle and attribution of strikes.
impact_rationale: It offers clear entertainment and practice value for human-agent delegation, communication, and trust, even if the audience is specialized.
impact_evidence: ABOUT explicitly calls it a game and compact practice arena for human-agent delegation.
Visible timed task board and completion states support a playable experience.
creativity_rationale: The human/agent role split, manual-only agent, scoped per-act tools, and bounded consequential action form a fresh and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: WebMCP is used as the wall between two players rather than as automation.
Tool list changes with acts and normal control authority remains with the human.
usability_note: Onboarding, timer, task board, and visible act structure suggest a usable game loop; fair-play enforcement is acknowledged as a caveat.
red_flags: The author admits the page cannot technically prevent an agent from looking at the screen.
No transcript, so exact invocation sequence is not independently readable.
standouts: Scoped tool lifecycle is integrated into act progression.
The game turns information asymmetry into the core mechanic.
advance_reason: Strong creative and leverage fit with coherent visible timed-game execution.

one_line: An in-browser algorithm practice workspace with deterministic tests, Socratic hints, and spaced repetition.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect coding state, run isolated Web Worker tests, offer progressive hints, and schedule review locally.
leverage_rationale: Typed test execution and synchronized editor/session state materially improve reliability over an agent guessing through a coding UI, though coding-coach functionality itself is familiar.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT describes run_tests, get_hint, get_recommendation, clientState, and Web Worker execution.
Devpost screenshot claims deterministic assertions, hard CPU-loop timeout, and local IndexedDB/SM-2.
execution_rationale: Frames show a coding-coach landing page, editor/workspace, execution controls, and preference configuration; the packet does not clearly show a completed test result or full coaching turn.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show Client-Side Coding-Coach landing, multi-panel coding workspace, code/editor content, and Visit Preferences form.
Devpost packaging aligns the product, tools, sandbox, and local storage claims.
No gallery images are reported.
impact_rationale: Coding interview candidates and learners have a clear need for reliable execution feedback and hints that do not spoil solutions; the described features address both pain points.
impact_evidence: ABOUT identifies hallucinated code assessment and solution dumping as the target problems.
Socratic hints, deterministic tests, and spaced repetition directly map to learner needs.
creativity_rationale: A strong, thoughtful synthesis of existing coding practice patterns with browser-native execution and agent coaching, but not as novel as the game/story concepts.
creativity_evidence: Combines progressive hints, isolated client-side execution, live state synchronization, and deterministic spaced repetition.
Zero-account local learning loop is a notable implementation choice.
usability_note: The landing, workspace, and preference screens imply a structured learning flow, but outcome states are not fully evidenced.
red_flags: No transcript and no gallery images.
Frame sheets show workspace and preferences but not a clearly legible completed test/coaching result.
standouts: Deterministic in-browser execution addresses a real agent reliability failure mode.
advance_reason: Solid product and impact, but lower novelty and incomplete end-to-end evidence relative to stronger packets.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured shared state, named role requests, evidence-linked writes, revision checks, safe retries, and exact decision retrieval; generic UI driving would be less reliable.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT lists seven tools including boardroom context, perspectives, contributions, recommendations, and decision record.
Mutations use expectedRevision and operationId for optimistic concurrency and safe retries.
Description emphasizes live brief and visible human-controlled decision workflow.
execution_rationale: Frames show a consistent request/review/approval-style application with sidebar records, structured forms, warning states, populated fields, and activity history; the six-perspective outcome is not clearly legible in the frames.
execution_evidence: Contact sheet shows request navigation, central form, warning banner, green completion states, and right-side activity/comments.
ABOUT describes budget revision from R20,000 to R8,000 and preserved decision record.
Devpost screenshot identifies the product and seven native tools.
impact_rationale: Founders and teams have a real need to organize multi-perspective decisions under changing constraints; visible revision and approval records directly address traceability.
impact_evidence: ABOUT names six decision roles and a changed launch budget scenario.
Human approval/reject/request-revision controls and evidence-linked contributions are described.
creativity_rationale: The stateful boardroom metaphor and role-based single-agent workflow are a fresh synthesis, though decision-support rooms are a known category.
creativity_evidence: One agent adopts six specialist perspectives while the founder retains final decision authority.
Stale recommendations and revision-aware records are built into the interaction.
usability_note: The request list, form, activity panel, and approval actions suggest a comprehensible review flow, though the final boardroom view is not clearly shown.
red_flags: No video transcript and no gallery images.
Frame evidence shows a generic request workflow more clearly than the claimed six-role boardroom output.
standouts: Revision-aware decision records and evidence-linked role contributions.

one_line: A browser-native vector motion studio where agents manipulate scene state, keyframes, presets, and exports.

leverage_rationale: Typed access to scene/timeline state and imperative animation/export operations can substantially outperform coordinate-based UI automation for precise motion design, though manual editing remains possible.
leverage_evidence: ABOUT lists structured scene inspection, layer creation/refinement, keyframes, easing, spring physics, playback, and CSS/SVG/Lottie export.
Tool Stream records inputs, results, status, and execution time; manual and agent handlers are shared.
execution_rationale: Frames show a dark multi-pane development/editor workflow with code, prompts, configuration, modals, and generated form-like interface, but do not clearly expose the claimed motion timeline/canvas output.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show repeated multi-pane editor/configuration screens, code/file views, generation controls, and form/dashboard output.
Devpost screenshot states vector motion studio, live canvas/timeline, tools, and exports.
No gallery images are reported.
impact_rationale: Motion designers have a concrete need for precise repetitive timeline work and multi-format export; the product plausibly reduces that labor.
impact_evidence: ABOUT describes repetitive timeline editing, precise layer targeting, and export steps as the target pain.
Claims include live preview, undo, and multiple standard animation exports.
creativity_rationale: Agent-native manipulation of vector scenes and timeline/keyframe state is an ambitious and useful creative-tool synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Combines visual human selection with structured agent motion work.
Includes spring physics, presets, SVG orchestration, and three export formats.
usability_note: The claimed shared canvas and Tool Stream suggest inspectability, but the submitted frames do not clearly show the final motion-design surface.
red_flags: No transcript and no gallery images.
Contact sheets emphasize a generic coding/configuration environment; motion canvas/timeline evidence is weak or illegible.
standouts: Strong agent/human division between pointing at a layer and authoring precise motion operations.
